result:
`bun run typecheck` passes and `bun test` is green (4 pass, 0 fail; the stack traces printed are the framework's pre-existing logging of handled 422s, present in the original suite too).

The bug was in `app/Http/Controllers/PostController.ts:96` — `update()` was the only action hand-rolling its redirect, returning `new Response(null, { status: 302, headers: { Location: ... } })`. A 302 does not tell the client to switch methods, so Inertia's fetch client re-issued the `PUT` against `/posts/<id>`, hit the same route, got another 302, and looped until the browser aborted with `ERR_TOO_MANY_REDIRECTS` — after the row had already been updated, which is why the edit appeared on reload. I replaced it with `this.redirect(\`/posts/${post.id}\`)`, the same helper `store()` and `destroy()` already use; it answers non-GET requests with 303, which turns the follow-up into a plain GET of the post page. Validation is untouched, so a bad payload still throws before the redirect and returns 422 to the form. I also added `tests/PostUpdate.test.ts`, which resets the test database, creates an author and a post, and asserts that an authenticated save returns 303 with `Location: /posts/<id>` and persists the new title, plus that an empty payload still returns 422.
